title: Cases for fixed-width increment
statement: For every Boolean word $x$, either $x$ consists entirely of true values and its fixed-width increment is undefined, or there are a natural number $j$ and a Boolean word $r$ such that $x$ is $j$ true values followed by false and then $r$, and its increment is $j$ false values followed by true and then $r$.
replaced:
Every word $x \in \{0,1\}^*$, read least-significant bit first, satisfies
exactly one of the following: $x$ consists entirely of ones and its
fixed-width increment overflows (is undefined); or $x = 1^j 0 r$ for some
$j \ge 0$ and tail $r$, and the fixed-width increment of $x$ is $0^j 1 r$.
